pk.context: 25 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: light red, film-coated, oval biconvex tablet

clues.kinetics: Absolute bioavailability is approximately 100%, and a high-fat meal does not significantly change exposure. About 20% is bound to plasma proteins, and 60% to 71% of the dose is excreted unchanged in urine.
clues.substance: A benzoate salt whose active moiety has molecular weight 339.4. A crystalline powder that is sparingly soluble in water.
clues.product: Marketed under an NDA in 6.25, 12.5 and 25 mg strengths.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated after serious hypersensitivity to it or its excipients; anaphylaxis, angioedema and severe skin reactions have been reported.
clues.indication: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes.
clues.mechanism: Selectively inhibits DPP-4, slowing the breakdown of incretin hormones such as GLP-1; in vitro, DPP-8 and DPP-9 are not inhibited.

tell: It inhibits DPP-4 but not DPP-8 or DPP-9 in vitro, and accumulates minimally on repeated dosing.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: (median T max ) occurred one to two hours after dosing
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: mean terminal half-life (t 1/2 ) of approximately 21 hours
